name: HackerTube top 50
description: The 50 YouTube videos Hacker News recommends most, by HackerTube's quality score.
credit: Picks from HackerTube (hackertube.org) by Andrej Karpathy, derived from the open-index/hacker-news dataset, ODC-By 1.0
notes: Ranked by HackerTube's score field. Summaries and why-HN-likes-it lines were written by an LLM for HackerTube and are trimmed here. Video titles and channel names belong to their creators. No durations: HackerTube does not redistribute YouTube metadata. Not affiliated with YouTube, Google, Hacker News or Y Combinator.

videos.title: Vectors | Chapter 1, Essence of linear algebra
videos.summary: The first chapter of 3Blue1Brown's Essence of Linear Algebra series, introducing vectors with animated geometric visuals. It begins a series that builds intuition for linear algebra from the basics.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN's go-to recommendation for learning linear algebra intuition, repeatedly credited with making concepts click and complementing textbooks.

videos.title: Ruby Conf 12 - Y Not- Adventures in Functional Programming by Jim Weirich
videos.summary: Jim Weirich's RubyConf 2012 talk derives the Y combinator step by step, live-coding in Ruby lambdas. It builds up an understanding of functional programming and lambda calculus from first principles.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN recommends it repeatedly as one of the best and most entertaining programming talks, and as the talk that makes the Y combinator click, even for people who do not use Ruby.

videos.title: Indistinguishable From Magic: Manufacturing Modern Computer Chips
videos.summary: A HOPE09 talk on how modern computer chips are manufactured, from 22nm transistors to ultra-clean fabs and the tricks used to pattern tiny features with light. It frames chipmaking as hacking electrical engineering and physics.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN repeatedly calls it the best in-depth introduction to IC manufacturing, a sense-of-awe talk by an independent engineer, while wishing for an updated version.

videos.title: How to Speak
videos.summary: Patrick Winston's long-running MIT lecture on public speaking teaches heuristic rules for talks. It covers how to start, use time and place, boards, props and slides, and how to inform, persuade and finish.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN treats it as the canonical, near-universally recommended lecture on giving talks and presentations.

videos.title: The spelled-out intro to neural networks and backpropagation: building micrograd
videos.summary: Andrej Karpathy's first Neural Networks: Zero to Hero lecture, which builds micrograd, a tiny autograd engine, from scratch in Python.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN treats it as the best starting point for really understanding backprop and neural nets, because Karpathy explains the why with intuition and builds everything in code.

videos.title: 8 Bit & '8 Bitish' Graphics-Outside the Box
videos.summary: Mark Ferrari, the LucasArts background artist, explains in a GDC 2016 talk how he draws 8-bit graphics. He covers color cycling and palette shifting to create complex animated scenery without frame animation.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN repeatedly recommends it as a master class in limited-palette pixel art and palette cycling, from an artist behind Loom and Monkey Island.

videos.title: How Python was Shaped by leaky Internals, Armin Ronacher, Flask framework
videos.summary: Armin Ronacher, creator of Flask, explains how CPython's internals and C API leak into the language's semantics. Using examples like the complexity of the add operation, he shows why Python is hard to optimize or reimplement.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: It is HN's standard answer to why Python cannot easily get much faster, and is recommended by people who work on JITs and alternative runtimes.

videos.title: AT&T Archives: Similiarities of Wave Behavior (Bonus Edition)
videos.summary: A Bell Labs film in which Dr. J.N. Shive uses a mechanical wave machine to demonstrate reflection, standing waves, resonance and impedance matching. He includes some equations but relies mostly on real-world examples a layperson can follow.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN repeatedly calls it the clearest introduction to waves and transmission-line behavior, better than modern explainers.

videos.title: In Search Of A Flat Earth
videos.summary: Dan Olson's 76-minute essay on flat earth belief, built around a hike to a lake to test earth's curvature. It examines the community, how YouTube promoted it, and how it connects to wider conspiracy thinking and QAnon.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN treats it as the definitive, compassionate documentary on why people fall into conspiracy theories.

videos.title: 1. Introduction to Human Behavioral Biology
videos.summary: The opening lecture of Robert Sapolsky's Stanford course on Human Behavioral Biology, explaining the course premise and how to avoid categorical thinking.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: One of the most consistently recommended lecture series on HN, praised as fascinating, funny and eye-opening about human behavior across many scales.

videos.title: How The Economic Machine Works by Ray Dalio
videos.summary: Ray Dalio's 30-minute animated video explains how the economy works through credit, debt, interest rates, and short- and long-term cycles. It is based on his template for understanding the economy.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN repeatedly recommends it as the best layperson overview of debt, credit and economic cycles.

videos.title: RailsConf 2014 - All the Little Things by Sandi Metz
videos.summary: Sandi Metz takes an ugly section of conditional code and refactors it into a few simple objects, bridging object-oriented theory and practice.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN treats it as a top-tier programming talk for learning refactoring and for the wrong-abstraction principle, recommended repeatedly over a decade.

videos.title: But what is the Fourier Transform? A visual introduction.
videos.summary: 3Blue1Brown's animated visual introduction to the Fourier Transform, showing how a signal breaks into frequency components.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN's default recommendation for understanding the Fourier transform intuitively; many say it was the explanation that made it click.

videos.title: Around The Corner - How Differential Steering Works (1937)
videos.summary: A 1937 GM-produced film explaining how the automobile differential lets wheels turn at different speeds around a corner. It uses clear animations and cutaway demonstrations to build the idea from first principles.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: Held up as a marvel of pedagogy and the best explanation of differentials, recommended again and again.

videos.title: The Soul of Erlang and Elixir • Sasa Juric • GOTO 2019
videos.summary: Sasa Juric explains what makes Erlang and Elixir suited to server-side systems, focusing on the BEAM concurrency model rather than syntax or ecosystem. He demonstrates processes, supervision, and fault tolerance.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: It is HN's favorite pitch for Elixir and the BEAM, credited with convincing many people to adopt them.

videos.title: Essential Ideas for Parents
videos.summary: Dr. Russell Barkley's roughly three-hour lecture on ADHD for parents of affected children. It explains what ADHD is and how the ADHD brain differs.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: Repeatedly called the best way to understand ADHD, and recommended to anyone before commenting on it.

videos.title: "Simple Made Easy" - Rich Hickey (2011)
videos.summary: Rich Hickey's Strange Loop 2011 keynote distinguishing 'simple' (not intertwined) from 'easy' (familiar or near at hand). It argues that software complexity comes from complecting things and that we should pick simple constructs.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN treats it as the canonical talk on software complexity, shared constantly and recommended to every programmer regardless of language.

videos.title: The Quantum Conspiracy: What Popularizers of QM Don't Want You to Know
videos.summary: Ron Garret's Google Tech Talk argues that quantum mechanics is no harder to understand than relativity and that popular accounts wrongly rely on the Copenhagen interpretation.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN commenters repeatedly recommend it as the talk that finally made quantum mechanics click, especially for programmers.

videos.title: Try to Rule Fairly and You'll Be Overthrown
videos.summary: CGP Grey's animated adaptation of The Dictator's Handbook, explaining how rulers stay in power by keeping a small group of key supporters happy rather than ruling fairly. It lays out selectorate theory and how resources shape regimes.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN treats it as the standard short summary of how power and political incentives work, applied to governments, companies and workplaces.

videos.title: LEADERSHIP LAB: The Craft of Writing Effectively
videos.summary: Larry McEnerney of the University of Chicago Writing Program gives a graduate-student session on writing effectively. His core idea is that readers care about value to them, not the writer's thinking process.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN users repeatedly say it changed how they think about writing, calling it a masterclass useful far beyond academia.

videos.title: What the heck is the event loop anyway? | Philip Roberts | JSConf EU
videos.summary: Philip Roberts explains the JavaScript event loop, call stack, callbacks and asynchronous behavior with live visualizations using a tool he built. It demystifies terms like non-blocking and single-threaded.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN commenters repeatedly name it as the best explanation of the JS event loop and the first thing to watch before tackling async code.

videos.title: But what is a neural network? | Deep learning chapter 1
videos.summary: 3Blue1Brown's first chapter on deep learning explains what neurons and layers are and the math underlying a basic neural network, using handwritten digit recognition with visual animations.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN treats it as the standard first stop for learning neural networks, praised for making the math intuitive.

videos.title: A Better Default Colormap for Matplotlib | SciPy 2015 | Nathaniel Smith and Stéfan van der Walt
videos.summary: SciPy 2015 talk by Nathaniel Smith and Stefan van der Walt on choosing a new default colormap for Matplotlib. It covers why Jet misleads, how perceptual color spaces work, and how viridis was designed.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN's go-to recommendation for colormap and color-perception questions; commenters call it funny, brief, clear and a favorite talk.

videos.title: George Lakoff: Moral Politics
videos.summary: Cognitive scientist George Lakoff lectures on how political debates are framed through language and metaphors tied to values, and on the moral worldviews behind progressive and conservative politics. It was given in 2005 at UC San Diego.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN commenters repeatedly say it changed how they hear political speech and recommend it for understanding why opponents are not simply stupid.

videos.title: Heat Pumps: the Future of Home Heating
videos.summary: Technology Connections explains how heat pumps work as reversed air conditioners and why they can deliver several times the heat of resistive heating per unit of energy. It also tackles common myths such as poor cold-weather performance.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN's default recommendation for a friendly, thorough introduction to heat pumps and why they are so efficient.

videos.title: Micro Men - 720p (2009)
videos.summary: Micro Men is a 2009 BBC comic drama about the early 1980s British home computer boom. It follows the rivalry between Clive Sinclair and Acorn founder Chris Curry over the BBC Micro contract and the ZX Spectrum.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN recommends it often as an entertaining and authentic dramatization of Sinclair versus Acorn, the story from which ARM grew.

videos.title: The Beauty of Bézier Curves
videos.summary: Freya Holmer explains how Bezier curves work, from the helper-line construction to their uses in animation, text rendering and shapes. It uses visuals from her Unity Shapes plugin and was a SoME1 contest winner.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN repeatedly calls it one of the best math and graphics explainers on YouTube, praised for bridging game dev and math.

videos.title: The Century of the Self (Full Adam Curtis Documentary)
videos.summary: Adam Curtis' multi-part documentary on how Freud's ideas and Edward Bernays' public relations shaped consumer culture and political control. It argues that business and government learned to manufacture desires.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN recommends it often and strongly as an eye-opening account of marketing psychology and the engineering of consumer society.

videos.title: The Tragedy of systemd
videos.summary: FreeBSD developer Benno Rice traces the history of init and bootstrap systems at linux.conf.au 2019 to explain why systemd was seen as necessary and why it provokes such strong reactions. He also discusses why change is scary.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: The most-recommended balanced take on systemd, from a BSD perspective, handed to anyone caught up in the systemd debate.

videos.title: Rich Harris - Rethinking reactivity
videos.summary: Svelte creator Rich Harris explains moving reactivity into the compiler and language rather than tracking state at runtime, with a history of spreadsheets as reactive systems and comparisons to React.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: The most recommended introduction to Svelte, credited with sparking its adoption.

videos.title: "Making Impossible States Impossible" by Richard Feldman
videos.summary: Richard Feldman's elm-conf talk on designing models so that bugs from impossible application states cannot occur, using Elm's compiler and types. It demonstrates techniques for making invalid states unrepresentable.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN repeatedly recommends it as a talk that changed how people model data, with ideas that apply well beyond Elm to any typed language.

videos.title: Dominion (2018) - full documentary [Official]
videos.summary: Dominion is a two-hour documentary using drones and hidden cameras to expose conditions in animal agriculture, including food, clothing, entertainment and research. It questions humanity's dominion over animals.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN commenters push it, often forcefully, as the video to watch to see what factory farming really involves, and some say it changed their diet.

videos.title: D/A and A/D | Digital Show and Tell (Monty Montgomery @ xiph.org)
videos.summary: Monty Montgomery of Xiph.org gives real-time demonstrations of sampling, quantization, bit depth and dither using real audio equipment, including both digital analysis tools and vintage analog bench gear.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN calls it the gold-standard debunking of audiophile myths and the stair-step misconception, and recommends it as a primer on digital audio.

videos.title: SM64 - Watch for Rolling Rocks - 0.5x A Presses (Commentated) [OUTDATED]
videos.summary: Pannenkoek2012's commentated tool-assisted Super Mario 64 run collecting the Watch for Rolling Rocks star with half an A press, using parallel universes and QPU movement. The video is marked outdated in favor of a newer version.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: Held up as a legendary deep dive into game internals, explained lucidly and with humor, and a gateway to the channel.

videos.title: 8-bit computer update
videos.summary: Ben Eater's short update announcing his plan to build another 8-bit computer from scratch on camera. It kicks off the breadboard computer series that became widely known.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN repeatedly recommends the series it launched as the best way to understand how a CPU works, praised for Eater's clear teaching.

videos.title: MIT's Pathway to Fusion Energy (IAP 2017) - Zach Hartwig
videos.channel: MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center
videos.summary: Zach Hartwig of MIT introduces the key concepts of magnetic fusion energy and the state of fusion research.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: Recommended again and again as the best accessible overview of fusion physics, useful for judging fusion announcements and understanding why high-temperature superconducting magnets matter.

videos.title: Stanford's Sapolsky On Depression in U.S. (Full Lecture)
videos.summary: Stanford professor Robert Sapolsky lectures on depression as a real biological disease. He covers its biological and psychological causes, how it differs from ordinary sadness, and ideas such as learned helplessness.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN returns to it repeatedly as the best single introduction to understanding clinical depression.

videos.title: The Continuity of Splines
videos.summary: Freya Holmer's 74-minute video essay on splines, covering Bezier curves, B-splines, derivatives and the different levels of continuity (C0, C1, C2), built with custom animation tools. She notes she did not cover non-uniform splines.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: It is the go-to recommendation for anyone who wants to genuinely understand Bezier curves and splines, and commenters repeatedly call it one of the best programming-related educational videos.

videos.title: Justice: What's The Right Thing To Do? Episode 01 "THE MORAL SIDE OF MURDER"
videos.summary: The first episode of Michael Sandel's Harvard course on moral reasoning, opening with the trolley problem and the choice between killing one to save five.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: One of the most frequently recommended online lecture series on HN, praised for giving people vocabulary to examine ethical positions and for Sandel's skilled teaching.

videos.title: Video explains the world's most important 6-sec drum loop
videos.summary: Nate Harrison's 2004 video history of the Amen Break, a six-second drum sample from a 1969 b-side that became the basis of hip-hop sampling, jungle and drum and bass. It is also a meditation on cultural ownership and creativity.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: A perennial HN recommendation, brought up whenever sampling, copyright or music history comes up, often described as a must-watch.

videos.title: CppCon 2015: Andrei Alexandrescu “std::allocator...”
categories: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages
videos.summary: Andrei Alexandrescu's CppCon 2015 talk argues that std::allocator is badly designed. He proposes building high-performance allocators from small composable, templated pieces.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN repeatedly recommends it as an entertaining, mind-opening talk on allocator design and composable generic programming.

videos.title: Jim Simons (full length interview) - Numberphile
videos.summary: The full-length Numberphile interview with mathematician and hedge fund founder Jim Simons.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN recommends it as the best readily available interview with Simons, notable for his emphasis on luck and a humble approach to success.

videos.title: Reverse emulating the NES to give it SUPER POWERS!
videos.summary: Tom Murphy (suckerpinch) shows 'reverse emulation', using a Raspberry Pi in an NES cartridge to give an unmodified NES new abilities such as playing SNES games. The video starts in a strange way and gets stranger.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: Praised as a brilliant, deadpan and inventive hardware hack, and a good starting point for Tom7's videos.

videos.title: Sugar: THE BITTER TRUTH
videos.summary: Robert Lustig of UCSF lectures on the biochemistry of sugar, arguing that fructose and lack of fiber drive the obesity epidemic via insulin. It is the widely viewed 90-minute talk that popularized the anti-sugar case.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: The most-linked YouTube video on HN, recommended as an in-depth explanation of fructose metabolism.

videos.title: Designing the Ideal Bootstrapped Business with Jason Cohen
videos.summary: Jason Cohen's MicroConf talk on designing a bootstrapped business by starting from your own strengths, goals and constraints.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: It is the go-to talk HN commenters recommend to anyone asking about bootstrapping, SaaS pricing, or choosing bootstrapping over VC.

videos.title: How Self-Driving Cars will Destroy Cities (and what to do about it)
videos.summary: Not Just Bikes argues that self-driving cars will worsen sprawl and car dependence and harm cities. The video compares car-centered and people-centered urban design and weighs what cities should do instead.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: Frequently recommended in autonomous vehicle and Waymo threads as the main counterargument, a long but worthwhile video essay on how self-driving cars could affect cities.

videos.title: Light Years Ahead | The 1969 Apollo Guidance Computer
videos.summary: Robert Wills of TNMoC explains the Apollo Guidance Computer hardware and software, then walks through the Apollo 11 landing procedure step by step, including the 1202 alarms.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN calls it mandatory viewing on the AGC, praising the speaker's enthusiasm and the clear account of restartable, robust software design.

videos.title: Steve Jobs Stanford Commencement Speech 2005
videos.summary: Steve Jobs's 2005 Stanford commencement address, built around three stories: connecting the dots, love and loss including being fired from Apple, and death. It is a 15-minute talk on finding work you love.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: HN returns to it for years as an inspirational talk to send to graduates, founders and anyone at a career crossroads.

videos.title: Quantum Computing for Computer Scientists
videos.summary: An 88-minute Microsoft Research talk that explains how quantum computers beat classical ones using basic linear algebra, qubits, superposition and gates.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: It is HN's most frequently recommended starting point for quantum computing because it avoids pop-science hand-waving and needs only basic linear algebra.

videos.title: Juice it or lose it - a talk by Martin Jonasson & Petri Purho
videos.summary: Martin Jonasson and Petri Purho take a bland Breakout clone and add layer after layer of 'juice' such as easing, particles, screen shake and sound until it feels alive. A live demo makes the effect of small feedback details obvious.
videos.why_hn_likes_it: The go-to recommendation on game feel and polish, cited by HN as one of the best talks for anyone making interactive things feel good.
